subject: chemistry
topicDisplay: Structure 1 · Atomic Structure (Particulate Nature, Nuclear Atom, Electron Configurations)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which state of matter has particles that are close together but able to move past one another?
questions.explain: In liquids particles are close but mobile; solids are fixed in a lattice and gases are far apart and fast-moving.

questions.q: The change of state directly from solid to gas is called:
questions.explain: Sublimation is solid → gas (e.g. solid CO2); deposition is the reverse.

questions.q: During melting, the temperature of a pure substance stays constant because the heat energy is used to:
options: Overcome forces between particles rather than raise kinetic energy
questions.explain: At a change of state, energy breaks intermolecular forces, so temperature is constant until the change is complete.

questions.q: The subatomic particle with a relative charge of +1 is the:
questions.explain: Protons are +1, electrons -1, and neutrons are neutral.

questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have:
options: The same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
Different numbers of electrons when neutral
questions.explain: Isotopes share atomic number (protons) but differ in neutron number, so they have different mass numbers.

questions.q: An atom has 17 protons, 18 neutrons and 17 electrons. Its mass number is:
questions.explain: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 17 + 18 = 35 (this is chlorine-35).

questions.q: The relative atomic mass of an element is:
options: The weighted mean mass of its isotopes relative to carbon-12
The mass of its most common isotope
questions.explain: It is a weighted average of isotope masses by their abundance, so it is often non-integer.

questions.q: Chlorine has isotopes Cl-35 (75%) and Cl-37 (25%). Its relative atomic mass is approximately:
In a mass spectrometer, particles are separated according to their:
questions.explain: Ions are deflected according to their m/z, allowing isotopes to be identified and their abundances measured.

questions.q: Emission line spectra provide evidence that electrons in atoms:
questions.explain: Lines correspond to electrons falling between fixed energy levels, emitting specific wavelengths.

questions.q: As energy levels increase (moving away from the nucleus), the lines in an emission spectrum:
questions.explain: Energy levels get closer at higher n, so the spectral lines converge towards the series limit.

questions.q: The maximum number of electrons that the second main energy level can hold is:
questions.explain: Level 1 holds 2, level 2 holds 8 (2 in 2s, 6 in 2p).

questions.q: The full electron configuration of a neutral sulfur atom (Z = 16) is:
questions.explain: 16 electrons fill up to 3p4 following the Aufbau principle.

questions.q: The Aufbau principle states that electrons:
options: Fill the lowest available energy sub-levels first
Pair up before occupying separate orbitals
Have identical spin in an orbital
questions.explain: Electrons occupy the lowest-energy orbitals available before higher ones.

questions.q: A single orbital can hold a maximum of:
questions.explain: By the Pauli exclusion principle, an orbital holds at most two electrons of opposite spin.

questions.q: The condensed electron configuration of calcium (Z = 20) is:
questions.explain: After the argon core (18 electrons), the two remaining electrons enter the 4s sub-level.

questions.q: An ion with more electrons than protons carries:
questions.explain: Gaining electrons gives a net negative charge (an anion); losing electrons gives a cation.

questions.q: Within the same sub-level, electrons occupy separate orbitals singly before pairing. This is:
questions.explain: Hund's rule minimises repulsion by keeping electrons unpaired in degenerate orbitals where possible.

questions.q: Which of the following is a physical property that supports the kinetic molecular theory of gases?
options: Gases are easily compressed because particles are far apart
questions.explain: Large spaces between gas particles allow compression and rapid diffusion.

questions.q: A magnesium ion Mg2+ has how many electrons? (Z of Mg = 12)
questions.explain: Mg loses two electrons to form Mg2+, leaving 12 − 2 = 10 electrons.
